Build a validated parameter set for the vivax model

Source: R/params.R
vivax_params.Rd

Returns a named list of all model parameters, starting from the defaults (which mirror the SLiM model) and overriding any you name. SEED and OUTDIR are set by run_sim(), not here.

Usage

vivax_params(...)

# S3 method for class 'vivax_params'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

...

named parameter overrides, e.g. N_HOSTS = 300, BITING_RATE = 0.09; ignored by as.data.frame().

x

a vivax_params object.

row.names, optional

ignored.

Value

a named list of every model parameter (class vivax_params): the defaults with your overrides, checked. print() shows the values that differ from the defaults, and as.data.frame() gives the table: name, value (as SLiM is given it), default, changed, group, unit and meaning.

Details

The defaults are an illustrative preview, 40 hosts for a year, not a calibrated setting: at them the relapse rate is above its calibration target even with NU_HYPNOZOITE_BATCH = 3. NU_HYPNOZOITE_BATCH = 3 is the value fitted to four calibration targets, ranges taken from published P. vivax studies, at moderate transmission (BITING_RATE 0.08 with 2 mosquitoes per host and 400 hosts): section 13 of the model description gives the targets and their sources, and inst/validation/calibrate_nu.R repeats the fit. Re-fit it when transmission or scale change, since both move the relapse rate. BITING_RATE, with N_MOSQ / N_HOSTS, sets the transmission intensity and is for each study to choose.

Time is in days: one model tick is one day. A duration parameter D (such as MEAN_BLOOD_STAGE_DURATION or MOSQ_LIFESPAN) is the mean of a geometric duration: the event happens each day with probability 1/D. The treatment delay (TREATMENT_DELAY) and, under the default RECRUD_DELAY_DIST = "geometric", the recrudescence delay (MEAN_RECRUD_DELAY) follow the same rule from the day after the case or the suppression, so they are at least one day; EIP_DAYS and GAMETOCYTE_DELAY are fixed delays. Rates (BITING_RATE, ALPHA_ACTIVATE, MU_HYPNOZOITE, DELTA_LATENCY) are daily probabilities; a mosquito bites at most once a day, so the realised biting rate is capped at 1, and vivax_params() warns when the peak over the run, with its seasonal, intervention and resurgence multipliers, passes it.

Values the model cannot run are refused here, before SLiM starts, naming the parameter; the Parameters section below gives what each may be, and param_info() the same as a table. Each value is a number, TRUE/FALSE or a string, as its default is; numbers are finite, and strings are UTF-8 text without control characters. The tables are also in section 10 of the model description.

Several sizes are capped far above anything realistic, so a cap binds only on an absurd value; each parameter's row below gives its own, uptake_moments() the oocyst one. A founder-free run whose imports never establish a parasite, by chance or because its settings let none take, is not refused here; it ends as never started (see load_run()). Imports arrive on days 1 to SIM_DAYS: a pulse or an import window set outside the run brings nothing, without a warning, which is how imports are switched off in one arm of a grid. Each host takes at most one import a day, so a day's imports beyond N_HOSTS never arrive. This warns when a day's fixed imports inside the run exceed N_HOSTS (N_IMPORTS on IMPORT_TICK, N_IMPORTS_PER_TICK in the window, or both on the same day), and when IMPORT_RATE_PER_TICK at its peak over the window, with its seasonal and resurgence multipliers and with N_IMPORTS_PER_TICK, draws more than N_HOSTS imports on a day with probability above 0.01.

Each value is stored as its default's type and as SLiM is given it (a double to the 15 significant digits run_sim() passes), so a set rebuilt from a run's params.tsv is the set it used. Common forms are converted, such as a named number or a whole number carrying floating-point noise; a number of another class, such as a bit64::integer64, is refused: give the number itself.

Editing a set. A set edited with $<-, [[<- or modifyList() keeps its class and is not checked at the edit. It is checked in full when it is used: run_sim() and run_grid() build every set again through vivax_params(), and p <- do.call(vivax_params, p) checks it at once. A default taken from another parameter is set only when a set is built, so editing N_FOUNDER_HOSTS leaves N_FOUNDER_LINEAGES as it was.

Choosing a value. The parameters below give their bounds and, where a value is easy to get wrong, a Setting: note on how to choose one. vignette("parameters") collects those notes and the cross-parameter advice they depend on, such as the scale dependence of transmission.

See also

param_info(), run_sim(), load_params(), uptake_calibrate()

Parameters

Every parameter, by group. Section 10 of the model description holds the same tables.

Run

Length, label and what is recorded.

SIM_DAYS

Length of the run; one tick is one day. A run that goes extinct, or never starts, ends sooner. Unit: days. Default 365; whole number in [2, 1e9]; a run that reaches day 99999 must move the days that default to 99999 past its end.

SIM_ID

A label for the run, written into params.tsv. Default "default"; text; UTF-8, without control characters.

VERBOSE

Narrate every event in run.log. The outputs are the same either way. Default FALSE; TRUE or FALSE.

RETAIN_FULL_HISTORY

Keep every genome in the tree sequence, which IBD to infections that have already cleared needs. With FALSE most earlier genomes leave the tree, and ibd_pairs() warns that the ids it was asked about are absent; they look up as NA. Default TRUE; TRUE or FALSE.

Population

Hosts, mosquitoes and the founding infections.

N_HOSTS

Humans; the number is constant. Unit: hosts. Default 40; whole number >= 1. Setting: prevalence and COI are scale-dependent, so a transmission rate fitted at one population size does not transfer: calibrate at the size you will publish (roadmap S10).

N_MOSQ

Mosquitoes; the number is constant, and every one starts uninfected. Unit: mosquitoes. Default 100; whole number >= 1. Setting: the transmission rate depends only on BITING_RATE x N_MOSQ / N_HOSTS, so the two trade off, but the genetics do not: spreading the same uptakes over more mosquitoes lowers co-transmission. Hold it fixed and vary BITING_RATE where a result turns on co-transmission, and calibrate at publication scale (roadmap S10).

N_FOUNDER_HOSTS

Hosts infected at the start: establishment, whether the epidemic sustains itself. Unit: hosts. Default 12; whole number >= 0; at most N_HOSTS; 0 needs an import path inside the run. Setting: hold this fixed and vary N_FOUNDER_LINEAGES to change founding diversity without changing whether the epidemic establishes.

N_FOUNDER_LINEAGES

Distinct founding genomes among the founder hosts; the others carry clonal copies, seeded on day 2. The genealogical diversity knob: fewer lineages give higher background relatedness at the same establishment. Unit: genomes. Default N_FOUNDER_HOSTS; whole number >= 0; at most N_FOUNDER_HOSTS, and at least 1 when there are founder hosts. Setting: the clean genealogical diversity knob: lower it, at fixed N_FOUNDER_HOSTS, to raise background relatedness without changing establishment.

Transmission

Bites, infection and the mosquito's incubation.

BITING_RATE

Daily probability that a mosquito bites. Bites per human per day are BITING_RATE x N_MOSQ / N_HOSTS, not this value. Unit: per mosquito per day. Default 0.1; number > 0; a mosquito bites at most once a day, so it warns when the peak over the run, with its seasonal, intervention and resurgence multipliers, passes 1. Setting: the main transmission knob, but prevalence and complexity of infection are scale-dependent, so a value fitted on a small population does not transfer: calibrate it at the population size you will publish (roadmap S10).

P_TRANS_VH

b: an infectious bite infects the human. Unit: probability. Default 0.5; number in [0, 1].

P_TRANS_HV

c: a mosquito that bites an infectious human takes up parasites. Unit: probability. Default 0.5; number in [0, 1].

MOSQ_LIFESPAN

Mean mosquito lifespan: a mosquito dies each day with probability 1/MOSQ_LIFESPAN. Unit: days. Default 10; number >= 1.

EIP_DAYS

Extrinsic incubation period: days from uptake until a mosquito's products can be transmitted (fixed). Unit: days. Default 10; whole number >= 0.

MAX_MOI

A host already carrying this many blood-stage lineages, patent or subpatent, takes no new inoculation, counting the clones it gained earlier that day. Relapses bypass it, and a bite that delivers several genotypes is admitted whole. 1 means no superinfection; at 20 it is a guard that seldom binds. Unit: lineages. Default 20; whole number >= 1. Setting: a runaway guard, not a quantity to vary: at 20 it essentially never binds, and set low it becomes what you are measuring. Confirm it never bound in a published run (roadmap S8).

MAX_LINEAGES_PER_MOSQ

A mosquito carrying this many lineages takes up no more. One uptake can add up to four per oocyst, so the count can pass it. Unit: lineages. Default 20; whole number >= 0.

Blood stage

A clone's duration and its infectiousness to mosquitoes.

MEAN_BLOOD_STAGE_DURATION

Mean duration of a blood-stage clone: it clears each day with probability 1/MEAN_BLOOD_STAGE_DURATION. Unit: days. Default 60; number >= 1. Source: White et al. (2014). Setting: sets how much episodes overlap, and so polyclonality and the outcrossing that follows from it: sweep it when a result depends on COI or on relatedness within a host (roadmap S9).

P_PRIMARY

A transmitted genotype causes a blood-stage primary; its hypnozoite batch is drawn either way. Unit: probability. Default 1; number in [0, 1]. Source: White et al. (2014), base model.

P_GAMETOCYTE

An infection carries gametocytes, drawn once per infection. Vivax: about 0.9. Unit: probability. Default 1; number in [0, 1]. Setting: ships at 1, the identity: every infection is transmissible. Sweep a high but incomplete carriage of about 0.9 together with GAMETOCYTE_DELAY (roadmap S5).

GAMETOCYTE_DELAY

Days from blood-stage onset until a clone can infect mosquitoes (fixed). 0 acts as 1: a clone is first taken up the day after it appears. Vivax: about 2 to 3 days. Unit: days. Default 0; whole number >= 0. Setting: ships at 0, the identity: every blood-stage clone is transmissible at once. Vivax gametocytes appear early but not instantly, so sweep a short delay of about 3 days (roadmap S5).

Mosquito uptake and co-transmission

How many oocysts an uptake forms, and how many genotypes a bite delivers. Both lambdas are pre-truncation rates; 0 for both gives one oocyst per uptake and one genotype per bite, and the defaults let a bite co-transmit several.

LAMBDA_OOCYSTS

Pre-truncation rate of the zero-truncated number of oocysts per successful uptake, each its own meiosis; 0 gives exactly one, and the default a mean of 2.31. See uptake_moments() and uptake_calibrate(). Unit: oocysts. Default 2; number in [0, 1000]; with K_OOCYSTS, the mean count per uptake is at most 1000. Source: membrane feeds of wild An. arabiensis in Ethiopia give a median of 7.2 oocysts per midgut (Ayele et al. 2023). Setting: a rate before zero-truncation, not the mean oocysts a midgut carries: convert with uptake_calibrate() first. Vivax feeding counts are overdispersed and far higher than the default, so sweep it with K_OOCYSTS (roadmap S3).

K_OOCYSTS

Negative-binomial dispersion of the oocyst count (variance lambda + lambda^2 / K); 0 is Poisson. It applies to oocysts only. Vivax oocyst counts are overdispersed. Default 0; number >= 0; 0, or at least 0.001. Setting: leave at 0 for a Poisson count; raise it to match the overdispersion of vivax feeding studies, which the default does not have (roadmap S3).

LAMBDA_SPOROZOITES

Pre-truncation rate of the zero-truncated number of a mosquito's products an infectious bite samples, repeats of a lineage counted once, so a bite can deliver several genotypes; 0 gives one genotype per bite. No study has measured the genotypes a natural bite delivers, so the default is an assumption to sweep. Unit: products per bite. Default 2; number in [0, 1000]. Setting: a rate before zero-truncation, not the mean genotypes a feeding study reports: convert with uptake_calibrate() first. No measurement of genotypes per natural bite exists, so sweep it rather than trust a point value (roadmap S1).

Hypnozoite reservoir

The liver-stage batches a bite seeds, and their activation and death.

NU_HYPNOZOITE_BATCH

Mean of the geometric hypnozoite batch an infectious bite seeds, split over the genotypes it delivers. Fitted to four calibration targets at moderate transmission (section 13 of the model description); re-fit it per setting. Unit: hypnozoites per bite. Default 3; number in [0, 1e6]; times its boost, at most 1e6 once the trigger falls inside the run. Source: White et al. (2014), section 2. Setting: calibrated to 3 against relapse, molFOB, MOI and relapse-fraction targets for one setting, and it drives relapse rate, reservoir size and COI together: re-fit it per setting rather than carrying 3 over (roadmap S2).

ALPHA_ACTIVATE

Daily probability that a hypnozoite activates: a relapse. Unit: per hypnozoite per day. Default 1/170; number in [0, 1]. Source: an average carriage of about 170 days (Mehra et al. 2024b); White et al. (2014) estimate 1/332. Setting: with K_LATENCY, this sets relapse periodicity and so how identifiable a relapse is: report tropical and temperate settings separately rather than averaging them (roadmap S7).

MU_HYPNOZOITE

Daily probability that a hypnozoite dies, also while latent. Unit: per hypnozoite per day. Default 1/442; number in (0, 1]. Source: as in Mehra et al. (2024a), who credit White et al. (2014), whose table gives 1/425.

K_LATENCY

Latency stages a batch passes before it can activate: 0 is tropical, 2 temperate. Unit: stages. Default 0; whole number >= 0. Source: White et al. (2014). Setting: left at 0 the reservoir is tropical, with no delay before a hypnozoite can activate; 2 with DELTA_LATENCY gives the temperate pattern. Report the two separately (roadmap S7).

DELTA_LATENCY

Daily probability that a latent batch moves on one stage. Unit: per day. Default 1/100; number in (0, 1]; checked only when K_LATENCY > 0.

Genome

The neutral PvP01 genome the model simulates; the mutation rate is 0.

GENOME_MODE

"full": the 14 PvP01 chromosomes at full length (24.2 Mb); "core": each at 90% of its length, a placeholder for the core genome. Default "full"; "full" or "core".

CHROMOSOMES

Which PvP01 chromosomes to simulate, such as "1-14" or "1-3,5". Default "1-14"; text; chromosome numbers 1 to 14, each once, separated by commas, with low-high ranges.

RECOMB_RATE

Crossover rate within a chromosome; chromosomes assort independently. Run time grows steeply with it. Unit: per bp. Default -1; number <= 0.5; 0 or below means the default map rate, 7.4e-7. Source: Jiang et al. (2011).

Seasonality and vector control

Factors on the biting rate; seasonality also acts on the Poisson import rate.

SEASONAL_AMP

Amplitude A of the seasonal factor 1 + A cos(2 pi (t - SEASONAL_PHASE) / 365), floored at 0, on biting and on the Poisson import rate; 0 means no seasonality. Default 0; number >= 0.

SEASONAL_PHASE

Day of the year of the seasonal peak. Unit: day of the year. Default 0; number.

INTERVENTION_START

First day of vector control. Unit: day. Default 99999 (never); whole number.

INTERVENTION_END

Vector control acts on days INTERVENTION_START to INTERVENTION_END - 1. Unit: day. Default 99999 (never); whole number.

INTERVENTION_EFFICACY

Biting is multiplied by 1 - INTERVENTION_EFFICACY inside the window; importation and treatment are not affected. Unit: fraction. Default 0; number in [0, 1].

Detection and case management

A case is detected, decided where it arises and treated later, on the host; radical cure is nested in a blood-stage course. Off by default.

P_DETECT_PRIMARY

A primary infection or an import is detected, drawn once per bite (for all the genotypes it delivers) or per import. Unit: probability. Default 1; number in [0, 1].

P_DETECT_RELAPSE

A relapse is detected, drawn once per activation. Relapses are often subpatent, so a realistic value is lower. Unit: probability. Default 1; number in [0, 1]. Setting: relapses are often subpatent, and every observational result depends on this: sweep it over 0.15 to 1.0 rather than leaving it at the default of 1, which reports every relapse (roadmap S6).

BLOODCURE_COVERAGE

A detected case is treated: a course clears each patent clone the host carries, unless the clone survives. 0 turns the whole treatment path off. Unit: probability. Default 0; number in [0, 1].

P_BLOODCURE_SURVIVAL

A clone survives a course: a patent one, or under MDA a subpatent one too. Unit: probability. Default 0; number in [0, 1]. Source: about 0.10 in the literature.

RADCURE_COVERAGE

A treated case also gets radical cure: a probability given treatment, not a coverage of its own, so it does nothing unless BLOODCURE_COVERAGE > 0. Unit: probability. Default 0; number in [0, 1].

P_RAD_SURVIVAL

Radical cure fails: the patient's whole reservoir survives (RADCURE_MODE "person"), about 71% cure; or each hypnozoite survives ("hypnozoite"), where the same number would mean 95% efficacy. Unit: probability. Default 0.29; number in [0, 1]. Source: near the 70% effectiveness White et al. (2018) assume for a 14-day primaquine course, given poor adherence.

RADCURE_MODE

The unit of radical-cure failure: "person", or "hypnozoite", which thins the reservoir hypnozoite by hypnozoite and is the only mode that can clear part of it. Default "person"; "person" or "hypnozoite".

TREATMENT_DELAY

Mean days from a case to its course: geometric, at least one day, so a course never lands on the day the case arises. Unit: days. Default 7; number in [1, 1e6]. Source: White et al. (2014) use 7 days.

TREATMENT_START

First day on which a detected case can be prescribed a course; case management has its own window, separate from vector control. Unit: day. Default 0; whole number.

TREATMENT_END

Cases detected on days TREATMENT_START to TREATMENT_END - 1 are treated. The window gates the decision, not the delivery: a course prescribed before the end still arrives. Unit: day. Default 99999 (never); whole number.

Mass drug administration

One round, through the same course as case management.

MDA_TICK

Day of one MDA round, through the same course as case management: blood-stage drugs and radical cure, whatever RADCURE_COVERAGE is, for each host it reaches. It also reaches subpatent clones and clones that became patent that day, and it is not gated by the treatment window. Unit: day. Default 99999 (never); whole number; not 1 when a founder host carries a copy of another founder's genome.

MDA_COVERAGE

The round reaches a host, drawn for each host. Unit: probability. Default 1; number in [0, 1].

Recrudescence

A clone that survives a course can be suppressed below patency and return. Off by default.

P_RECRUD_GIVEN_FAIL

A clone that survives a course is suppressed below patency, to recrudesce later, rather than persisting. At 0 the third recurrence state is inert, which matches recrudescence being 0.2 to 0.3% of recurrences after chloroquine or artesunate. Unit: probability. Default 0; number in [0, 1]. Source: Taylor et al. (2019).

MEAN_RECRUD_DELAY

Mean days from suppression to recrudescence, at least one; a literature assumption pending parameterisation. Geometric at the default: a median of 7 days, about 94% within 28 days. Unit: days. Default 10.5; number in [1, 1e6]. Source: close to the prior of Taylor et al. (2019). Setting: a literature assumption rather than an estimate from data, and it sets how many recrudescences a 28-day follow-up sees: sweep it, though it matters only when P_RECRUD_GIVEN_FAIL is above 0 (roadmap S11).

RECRUD_DELAY_DIST

Shape of that delay: "geometric", the discrete form of an exponential delay; "poisson", 1 + Poisson(D - 1) with mean D, a tight-window sensitivity arm; or "fixed", round(D) days with halves rounded up (11 days at 10.5). Every shape is at least one day. Default "geometric"; "geometric" or "poisson" or "fixed".

P_DETECT_RECRUD

A recrudescence is detected; it should usually sit well below P_DETECT_PRIMARY. Unit: probability. Default 0.5; number in [0, 1]. Source: Ross et al. (2025) put recurrence detectability at 0.13 to 0.49 of a primary's.

SUBPATENT_INFECTIVITY

Infectiousness of a suppressed clone relative to a patent one. Neither 0 nor 1 is defensible. Unit: relative. Default 0.15; number in [0, 1]. Source: 0.035 to 0.10 in the model of White et al. (2018); 0.10 to 0.20 from the feeding studies compiled by Koepfli et al. (2021, Fig 5).

Resurgence

Multipliers that switch on from one day, to start a resurgence.

RESURGENCE_TRIGGER_TICK

Day from which the four boosts apply. Unit: day. Default 99999 (never); whole number.

BITING_RATE_BOOST

Multiplies BITING_RATE from the trigger. Unit: multiplier. Default 1; number >= 0.

ALPHA_ACTIVATE_BOOST

Multiplies ALPHA_ACTIVATE from the trigger, capped so that activation and death stay within one day's probability. Unit: multiplier. Default 1; number >= 0.

NU_HYPNOZOITE_BATCH_BOOST

Multiplies NU_HYPNOZOITE_BATCH from the trigger. Unit: multiplier. Default 1; number >= 0.

Importation

Three routes, which add up: a pulse, and a fixed daily count and a Poisson rate in a window. Each host takes at most one import a day, and a host at MAX_MOI takes none.

IMPORT_TICK

Day of one pulse of N_IMPORTS imports. Unit: day. Default 99999 (never); whole number.

N_IMPORTS

Size of the pulse. Unit: imports. Default 0; whole number >= 0; warns above N_HOSTS.

IMPORT_START

First day of the import window. Unit: day. Default 99999 (never); whole number.

IMPORT_END

Imports in the window arrive on days max(1, IMPORT_START) to min(IMPORT_END - 1, SIM_DAYS). Unit: day. Default 99999 (never); whole number.

N_IMPORTS_PER_TICK

A fixed number of imports on each day of the window. Unit: imports a day. Default 0; whole number >= 0; warns when a day's fixed imports exceed N_HOSTS.

IMPORT_RATE_PER_TICK

Mean of a Poisson number of imports on each day of the window; it follows the season. Unit: imports a day. Default 0; number in [0, 1e6]; at its seasonal and boosted peak, at most 1e6 a day.

IMPORT_RATE_BOOST

Multiplies IMPORT_RATE_PER_TICK from RESURGENCE_TRIGGER_TICK. Unit: multiplier. Default 1; number >= 0.

Examples

vivax_params(N_HOSTS = 300, BITING_RATE = 0.09, GENOME_MODE = "core")
#> <vivax_params> 63 parameters
#>   non-default:
#>     N_HOSTS                  = 300
#>     BITING_RATE              = 0.09
#>     GENOME_MODE              = core
p <- vivax_params(N_HOSTS = 300)
subset(as.data.frame(p), changed)
#>      name value default changed      group  unit
#> 5 N_HOSTS   300      40    TRUE Population hosts
#>                           meaning
#> 5 Humans; the number is constant.
